report.summary: The frontend Service has a misconfigured selector (app=frontend-broken-sre-eval) that matches zero pods, leaving the Service with no endpoints despite the frontend pod being healthy and actively serving requests.
report.root_cause: Service selector app=frontend-broken-sre-eval does not match any pod labels in the running frontend deployment. The Service looks for pods with the label app=frontend-broken-sre-eval, but the frontend pod lacks this label, resulting in endpoint_count=0 and making the Service unreachable.
evidence: get_service_status returned endpoint_count=0 and ready_endpoint_count=0 for frontend Service
get_workload_status shows frontend pod frontend-5dcf458cb5-rqkks is phase=Running with ready=true

get_pod_logs shows frontend application actively processing HTTP requests: POST /cart with http.resp.status 200, GET / with http.resp.status 200 and http.resp.took_ms ranging from 8–53ms, indicating the pod itself is healthy and responsive
Pod accumulated only 8 restarts since 2026-08-03T05:31:12Z (get_workload_status), with no recent CrashLoopBackOff or ImagePullBackOff, ruling out pod-level failures
alternatives: Frontend deployment pod template is missing the label app=frontend-broken-sre-eval that the Service expects (confidence 0.78): rejected because the Service selector name 'frontend-broken-sre-eval' is suspiciously self-descriptive with the word 'broken', suggesting the Service config (not the deployment) is intentionally wrong

A NetworkPolicy is silently blocking traffic to the frontend Service (confidence 0.12): rejected because endpoint_count=0 is a registration failure, not a traffic block; NetworkPolicies can only drop traffic between already-registered endpoints, they cannot prevent endpoint discovery

A recent rollout changed the deployment, removing or renaming the pod label (confidence 0.08): rejected because get_rollout_history shows all 4 revisions use identical image us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/google-samples/microservices-demo/frontend:v0.10.5, and the pod is Running/Ready (not CrashLoopBackOff), ruling out code or configuration changes in the rollout
report.impact: The frontend Service ClusterIP (10.43.7.76:80) is completely unreachable. Any client connecting to the Service will hang or timeout because no endpoints exist. The frontend pod is healthy and serving traffic internally, but is invisible to the Service routing layer. This breaks all external and inter-cluster traffic to the frontend.

remediation.action: Correct the frontend Service selector to match the actual pod labels in the deployment (expected to be app=frontend based on standard Kubernetes naming conventions).
remediation.rationale: The Service selector app=frontend-broken-sre-eval does not correspond to any pod label in the deployment. Standard Kubernetes convention uses app={deployment-name} as the pod label. Patching the selector to app=frontend will restore the Service-to-pod mapping and immediately register the healthy frontend pod as an endpoint, making the Service reachable.
